chunks: And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Husayn ibn Alwan, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:

When the month of Ramadan arrived, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood up, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'O people, Allah will suffice you against their enemy from the jinn.' And He said: 'Call upon Me, I will answer you,' and He promised you acceptance. Know that Allah has appointed seven angels for every rebellious devil so that none can overpower you until this month of yours ends. Know that the doors of heaven are opened from the first night of it, and that supplication in it is accepted.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits and divine promises associated with the month of Ramadan according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq emphasizes the unique spiritual atmosphere of Ramadan, where divine protection from jinn is guaranteed by seven angels per devil, ensuring uninterrupted worship. It highlights the metaphysical reality of opened heavenly gates and the certainty of answered supplications, reinforcing the month's status as a time of divine proximity and mercy in Shia tradition.
